THE VESSEL’S CARGO IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME. • USCG STATION LA/LB LAUNCHED A SURFACE ASSET TO ENFORCE A SAFETY ZONE NEAR THE ITS TERMINAL. • THERE IS NO REPORTED MEDIA INTEREST. • A FOLLOW-ON CIC WILL BE CONDUCTED AT 1800 EST / 2200 Z

Suspected Responsible Party: AMERICAN ENGINEERING & DEVELOPMENT

RESPONSIBLE PARTY WAS EXCAVATING A TRENCH TO INSTALL A WASTE LINE TO A STORM FIXTURE. GAS COMPANY LOCATOR MARKED THE LOCATION OF WHERE THEY THOUGHT A GAS LINE WAS LOCATED. RESPONSIBLE PARTY HAND EXCAVATED, POT HOLED AREA AND CALLED IN HIS OWN HYDROVAC TRUCK TO HELP LOCATE GAS LINE AND WAS STILL NOT ABLE TO FIND IT IN AREA MARKED BY GAS COMPANY. GAS LINE WAS 9'-0" FROM THE INDICATED LOCATE BOUNDARY RUNNING DIAGONALLY TO THE PARKING LOT INSTEAD OF DIRECTLY ACROSS IT. FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS SUMMONED, EVACUATED AREA PINCHED OFF PLASTIC GAS LINE BY FOLDING IT BACK AND TAPING IT OFF UNTIL GAS COMPANY COULD ARRIVE TO START REPAIRS.

Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 0.5 feet by 0.5 feet (area 0.25 sq. ft.)
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK (ALONG THE REVETMENT) ON AUGUST 29, 2011, SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708).

///WEB REPORT///BASED ON A MATERIAL BALANCE THE PLANT DOES NOT BELEIVE THAT WE EXCEEDED THE CONTINOUS RELEASE UPPERBOUND. THE PLANT HAS HAD SEVERAL UPPERBOUND EXCEEDANCES THAT COULD NOT BE JUSTIFIED. AN INVESTIGATION OF THE CEM SHOWED THAT LIQUID IS CONDENSING WITHIN THE SENSOR CAUSING ESTIMATION ERRORS. DURING FILM BREAKS THE H2S SPIKES AND THE HIGHER CONCENTRATION SATURATES THE LIQUID IN THE SENSOR. AFTER THE SPIKE IS REMOVED IT TAKES SEVERAL HOURS FOR THE LIQUID TO COME BACK TO EQUILLIBRIUM AT THE CURRENT SAMPLE CONDITION. ON 4-25-06 THE AMBIENT TEMPERATURE DROPPED BY 10 F OVER THE PREVIOUS DAY AND CASTING HAD SEVERAL FILM BREAKS WHICH CAUSED THE ERROR TO BE LARGE ENOUGH TO CAUSE THE APPARENT CONTINOUS RELEASE EXCEEDANCE. THE PLANT HAS SEEN OVER A 1000 LB/DAY DROP IN EMISSIONS AT THE SAME PRODUCTION RATE SINCE THE AMBIENT TEMPERATURE HAS RISEN. METHODS TO HEAT THE ENCLOSURE ARE CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED.

Nearest City: Belle Chasse, LA

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: CHEVRON ORONITE COMPANY
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 0.5 feet by 0.5 feet (area 0.25 sq. ft.)
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK (ALONG THE REVETMENT) ON JANUARY 11, 2011, SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708).
